d1.reason: Path A was reachable and is strictly better, so the code was fixed rather than the claim merely withdrawn: the panel's own data shows CME futures DO trade Columbus Day and Veterans Day (2020-10 has 22 bars for all 22 commodities against 22 weekdays), so a correct calendar is a fact about the data, not a judgement call. With the corrected calendar the 2020-10 counterexample is resolved with NO threshold change (MAX_RV_MONTH_SHORTFALL stays 1) and only ONE row changes in the whole panel. But Path A alone does not make the certification claim true, so the fourth falsified claim was withdrawn as well (partial Path B): a count-only cache still cannot see a one-day truncation common to every commodity, so `panel_span_is_complete_months_only` went true -> false and README's '3275 列皆為完整月份' was replaced by a screened-vs-certified distinction. Codex round 4: '若仍要認證完整月份，count-only frozen cache 需要獨立 endpoint 證據' -- that evidence does not exist in the frozen rv_monthly.csv, so the certification wording had to go regardless of how good the calendar is.
d1.code_change: K1694.py: `_expected_trading_days()` (weekdays - USFederalHolidayCalendar - GoodFriday) replaced by `_cme_trading_days()` -> `_expected_trading_days()`. The CME futures holiday set is New Year (observance=sunday_to_monday, i.e. NOT rolled back to 31 Dec when 1 Jan is a Saturday -- verified against 2010-12 and 2021-12, where every contract shows the extra day), MLK, Presidents' Day, Good Friday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth from 2022-06-19 (CME traded 2021-06-18), Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas. Columbus Day and Veterans Day are NOT subtracted. New module constant CME_UNSCHEDULED_CLOSURES enumerates the two sourced unscheduled closures and subtracts them day by day: 2012-10-29 and 2012-10-30 (Hurricane Sandy) and 2018-12-05 (national day of mourning for George H. W. Bush). No threshold was loosened: MIN_RV_DAYS=15, MAX_RV_SHORTFALL_VS_CALENDAR=2, MAX_RV_CROSS_SHORTFALL=2, MAX_RV_MONTH_SHORTFALL=1 are all unchanged; the corrected calendar makes the rule STRICTER (expected is now >= the old expected in every month). coverage_report() additionally enumerates, at run time, the months where max(ndays) exceeds the CME calendar because some contract prints an abbreviated holiday session -- that is exactly where the blind spot is 2 days rather than 1, and it is now published per month instead of being asserted away.

counterexample_2020_10.note: cross-sectional shortfall is 0 pre- and post-fix; the month-level calendar anchor is what catches it, which is why the anchor had to be correct.

d2.reason: The date-bearing path claimed to be a 'true endpoint test' while allowing three weekday gaps at each end, so it carried the very one-day blind spot it said existed only in the count-only cache. Withdrawing the claim (Path B) would have left a tolerance with no justification behind it; the tolerance existed only because there was no calendar to measure against. Once D1 supplied a correct calendar, an exact endpoint gate became available at no cost. The gate is written as an inequality against the calendar's endpoints rather than as strict equality, because the panel spans CME/CBOT/COMEX/NYMEX/ICE contracts whose holiday sessions differ: observing MORE than the calendar must not fail, observing LESS must always fail.
d2.code_change: K1694.py monthly_coverage(): the endpoint branch no longer measures gaps from the month boundary with a `.le(3)` tolerance. New `expected_month_endpoints()` returns the first and last scheduled CME trading day of each month (same calendar and whitelist as D1). rv_head_gap_days is now weekdays between the calendar's first trading day and the observed first_day; rv_tail_gap_days is weekdays between the observed last_day and the calendar's last trading day. The gate is `first_day <= expected_first AND last_day >= expected_last`, with zero tolerance; a contract that observes an abbreviated session outside the calendar reads a gap of 0 and passes. Missing endpoint dates still fail closed (.fillna(False)). The frozen count-only cache does not exercise this branch, which is stated in rule.rv_endpoint_test rather than glossed over.

sample.completeness.rule.rv_endpoint_test (dated cache): 'applied: observed first_day <= the calendar's first scheduled trading day of the month AND observed last_day >= its last, with no tolerance, so a truncation at either end fails whatever the day count says'

sample.completeness.rule.rv_residual_blind_spot: 'a truncation of exactly ONE day common to every commodity is indistinguishable, in a count-only cache, from an unscheduled market closure -- and by the same token an entry in rv_unscheduled_closures rests on the external event that dated it, not on anything this cache can show. Two such closures are in sample and are subtracted by name: 2012-10 (Hurricane Sandy) and 2018-12 (national day of mourning). This rule therefore does NOT prove each download reached both ends of its month; it SCREENS the day count for consistency with the CME futures calendar to within one day, wider by the excess shown in rv_months_observed_beyond_the_cme_calendar. Months that pass are screened, NOT certified complete: certifying them from a count-only cache would need independent endpoint evidence, which this frozen rv_monthly.csv does not carry.'

sample.panel_span_completeness_basis: 'every retained row's DCOT month is CERTIFIED continuous -- at least 4 reports, no gap over 9 days between consecutive reports including the entry gap from the previous month, so a skipped week anywhere fails. Its RV month is only SCREENED: the day count must match the CME futures calendar to within one day, which cannot rule out a one-day truncation common to every commodity. No partial month such as 2026-07 survives either test, but 'complete months only' would overstate the RV side. See sample.completeness.rule.rv_residual_blind_spot.'

residual_limitations: The reported run STILL rests on a count-only cache. A truncation of exactly one day common to all 22 commodities is invisible, and in the 6 months enumerated in rv_months_observed_beyond_the_cme_calendar it takes 3 days. The panel is therefore SCREENED, never certified complete. The exact-endpoint gate exists in code and is covered by tests, but the frozen rv_monthly.csv does not exercise it -- regenerating the cache from yfinance was deliberately not done, because provenance stability of the frozen input is worth more than upgrading the check, and the disclosure now says so instead of implying otherwise.

CME_UNSCHEDULED_CLOSURES is justified by external dated events (Hurricane Sandy 2012-10-29/30; national day of mourning 2018-12-05), not by anything this cache can prove. A whitelist entry is, by construction, indistinguishable from a common truncation in a count-only cache -- the same blind spot in another guise. This is stated inside rv_residual_blind_spot rather than left for a reviewer to notice.

No single fixed calendar predicts the daily-bar count of this panel exactly, and the code does not pretend one does. The panel spans CME/CBOT/COMEX/NYMEX/ICE contracts with differing abbreviated holiday sessions, and the provider's behaviour is not even stable over time: the 2016 Columbus Day and Veterans Day have no bar for any commodity, while the 2020 Columbus Day has one for all 22. Both directions of deviation are published per month rather than absorbed by a threshold.

The endpoint gate treats a missing first_day/last_day as failure. On a partially-dated cache that would mask months for want of metadata rather than for want of data. No such cache exists today; if one appears, that behaviour is a deliberate fail-closed choice and should be re-examined, not silently inherited.

Everything Codex passed in round 4 was left untouched and is therefore only as verified as it was then: estimator, provenance, NULL scope, DCOT entry-gap continuity, MAX_DCOT_GAP_DAYS separation, NOT SUPPORTED wording, bootstrap / shared sample / stationary bootstrap / t-2 adjacency / PIT regime timing.
conclusion_detail: VERDICT remains NULL: the negative, binary high-vol crowding-out interaction is NOT SUPPORTED. spec1 stays positive (wrong sign for the hypothesis) and insignificant: coef 3.103e-04 -> 3.097e-04, t_DK 1.53 -> 1.53, stationary-block bootstrap 95% CI still spans zero. spec2 (continuous rv_z) stays positive and significant, 2.880e-04 -> 2.875e-04, t_DK 2.55 -> 2.54, and is still named in verdict_scope so the NULL is not read wider than it is. spec4 stays near zero (t 0.28 -> 0.27). What moved is the disclosure, not the finding -- which is the same pattern as rounds 1-3: five rounds, four FAILs, and not one of them because the conclusion was wrong.
self_assessment: Both blocking defects are resolved in code, both counterexamples were reproduced on the pre-fix code (22/22 rows complete in each, exactly as Codex reported) and both now yield 0/22, and both regression tests demonstrably fail without the fix. The honest weak point is D1's status: the calendar is now correct as far as this panel's data can show, but 'correct' is not 'exact' -- no fixed calendar reproduces a multi-exchange panel's bar counts to the day, so I did not claim one does. Instead the rule's detection threshold is stated with its per-month exceptions enumerated at run time, and the certification claim that could not survive a count-only cache was withdrawn rather than defended. I expect the residual one-day blind spot to be the thing round 5 probes; it is disclosed in three places (rule.rv_residual_blind_spot, sample.panel_span_completeness_basis, README round-4 section) and pinned by tests, and closing it genuinely requires regenerating rv_monthly.csv with endpoint dates -- a trade against provenance stability that belongs to whoever owns that decision, not to this repair. Not done here and deliberately so: knowledge.json is untouched (K1259), the cache was not regenerated, nothing was merged, and the strict artifact check's single remaining finding is the knowledge entry this stage is forbidden to write.
